angle: retrieval side: query formulation under a matched result budget
study_sentence: A within-question comparison of three query-construction methods (verbatim question, deterministic keyword query set, LLM-written query set) on the set recall of a keyword scholarly-search API at a matched result budget, over the 597 LitSearch literature-search questions.
question: Does an LLM-written query set add at least 0.10 set recall on a keyword scholarly-search API beyond a deterministic keyword query set at a matched result budget?

original_question.text: How much does an LLM-written query set add to the set recall of a keyword scholarly-search API beyond a deterministic keyword query set at a matched result budget?
original_question.changed_because: restatement: the blind reader read a 'how much' question of which only one contrast is tested; the question is now the tested contrast with its threshold, and the sizes are named as estimates

inventory: ~/mne_data: EEG recordings only, no text-retrieval data
~/.cache/huggingface/hub: speech and EEG model checkpoints only, no instruct LLM and no dataset
LitSearch: not cached, public download needed
TREC-COVID: not cached, public download needed; serves as the second set with a share-of-relevant outcome

claims.statement: Although the recall gain of LLM-written queries over the verbatim question could come from shortening alone, an LLM-written query set exceeds a deterministic keyword query set by at least 0.10 set recall on a keyword scholarly-search API at a matched result budget, which we conjecture is because the LLM supplies terms that are not in the question.
reasons: An LLM can write terms absent from the question (synonyms, method names) that the gold paper's metadata contains
With the result budget equal, a difference in set recall can only come from the query strings

evidence.measure: set recall difference between the LLM-written query set and the deterministic keyword query set (five non-nested combinations of the six highest-IDF question words): API result ids per query -> union per question and arm -> h_q in {0,1} (any gold in the union) -> per-question difference -> mean over questions -> limits of the two-sided 90% paired bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples of questions)
evidence.would_show: lower limit of the interval of the difference at or above 0.10
evidence.refuted_if: upper limit of the two-sided 90% interval of the difference below 0.10
evidence.can_fail: yes: the manipulation acts on the query strings and the measure is computed on what the API returns for them; the difference can be negative, zero or positive depending on which terms the gold paper's metadata contains

construction.predictor_formula: u_qk = f_arm(x_q), k = 1..K  (the K query strings that method arm builds from question x_q; DET: five fixed 3- or 4-word combinations of the six highest-IDF words of x_q)
construction.outcome_formula: h_q = 1[G_q intersect UNION_k A(u_qk, R) is non-empty];  Delta = mean_q(h_q^LLM - h_q^DET)  with u_qk = f_arm(x_q)
construction.computable_without_experiment: no: after substitution h_q = 1[G_q intersect UNION_k A(f_arm(x_q), R) non-empty]; u_qk, x_q and f_arm stay inside A(.), an external search service whose response to a string is not in any existing table, and f_arm for the LLM arm is a model output that does not exist until it is generated
construction.free_quantity: which documents the API returns for each query string, and which words the gold paper's title and abstract contain

claims.warrant: When two query-construction methods are given the same number of queries and results on the same index, then a difference in recall of annotated gold papers measures what the query strings contribute.

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that an LLM contributes query content beyond shortening, so a literature agent's first step cannot be replaced by a keyword rule without losing recall
outcomes.if_not: we learn that most of the gain attributed to LLM query generation is reproduced by a deterministic rule, so the step can be made pure code and comparisons that type the question verbatim understate keyword search

negation.text: An LLM-written query set adds less than 0.10 set recall over a deterministic keyword query set at a matched budget.

expected_direction.direction: LLM at or above the deterministic keyword set
expected_direction.basis: contested: LLM-written expansions are reported to improve sparse retrieval [wangetal2023] (abstract, closed corpus), which predicts a positive increment; the conjunctive-matching account, under which any shortening of an over-long query recovers the loss, predicts an increment near zero

claims.smallest_effect_of_interest: 0.10 absolute set recall - design choice: below ten questions in a hundred an LLM call and its nondeterminism are not justified in a stage that can be pure code
claims.falsifier: E2: the upper limit of the two-sided 90% paired bootstrap interval of the set recall difference (LLM-written minus deterministic keyword query set) is below 0.10

rivals.how: more queries or more results return more papers, so recall rises whatever the wording
0/1 outcome per question on a few hundred questions

deterministic queries are built from the question's words through f_arm and the LLM may copy the same words, so u_qk can coincide in both arms and the difference is zero on those questions by construction
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: the query strings are the manipulation itself; E4 reports the share of questions with identical result sets and the difference outside them

rivals.how: the model has seen the gold paper for a LitSearch question and writes its title words
excluding questions whose gold is not indexed keeps the easier questions
unlabelled relevant papers count as misses under single-gold recall
query diversity: five free LLM queries may return more varied results than five deterministic queries built from one word list, whatever the terms are

controls.negative: E3: deterministic keyword queries of another question, same K and R, in two versions - another LitSearch question (fixed derangement; same field, so a conservative floor) and a TREC-COVID topic (unrelated field; a clean floor); expected mean h close to 0 for the unrelated-field version, both reported; aimed at the budget rival - a value above 0.05 means budget alone produces hits and E2 is reported net of it
controls.negative_can_move: yes: the control issues queries to the same API and h is computed on its results, so a large candidate set could contain the gold by popularity
controls.positive: E1: the gold paper's exact title as the query
controls.positive_expected: h is a 0/1 indicator averaged with its sign (no absolute value, rank or clip), so the planted effect returns unchanged: mean h at or above 0.95 on questions whose gold resolves to an OpenAlex work, provided title search ranks the work within R = 25; this value is also the ceiling of every arm

scope.internal: on LitSearch questions, OpenAlex search, K = 5 and R = 25, with small open instruct models (about 1.5B, and about 3B on a subset) and the harness's Step 1 prompt, we may claim whether the LLM increment over one deterministic keyword rule reaches 0.10
scope.external: generalises to keyword scholarly APIs with similar term matching; does not generalise to dense retrievers, to web search engines, to stronger generators or to agents that revise queries after reading results
limits: the because-clause (terms not in the question) is a conjecture; E4 reports term novelty but no rule tests it
one generator, weaker than the deployed one
a true increment between about 0.04 and 0.16 gives an undecided result by design
the comparator is one fixed deterministic rule; a better rule would lower the increment

power.min_detectable: against the threshold 0.10, one-sided alpha = 0.05, 80% power: a true increment is separated from 0.10 when it differs from it by at least 2.49 x SD / sqrt(550), i.e. 0.064 at SD 0.6 and 0.053 at SD 0.5 (refuted for a true increment up to about 0.04, supported from about 0.16, undecided between); against zero: d >= 0.11 SD

claims.statement: The gain in set recall of the deterministic keyword query set over the verbatim question on LitSearch questions is estimated with a 95% paired bootstrap interval.
reasons: the direction follows from term matching; the size is unknown

evidence.measure: mean over questions of h_q^DET - h_q^VERB at the matched budget, 95% paired bootstrap interval

claims.warrant: When the budget is equal, the difference in recall measures the effect of reducing a question to keywords.

outcomes.if_supported: a large gain means verbatim probing understates keyword search
outcomes.if_not: a small gain means the API tolerates long questions and the query form matters little

claims.estimate_because: size-open: the direction follows from conjunctive term matching (derivability screen); only the size is unknown
claims.precision_target: half-width of the 95% interval at most 0.05 with about 550 questions (a 0/1 difference has SD below 1, giving a half-width below 0.084 in the worst case; estimated, not timed)

claims.statement: Set recall is estimated as a function of the number of keywords per query (2 to 6) and of the number of queries (1, 2, 5) for each method.
reasons: shows where over-constraint starts and how much of any gain is the number of queries

evidence.measure: mean h_q per arm at each m and K, with 95% bootstrap intervals

claims.warrant: When only m or K changes, the change in recall measures that factor.

outcomes.if_supported: a peaked curve gives the keyword count to use
outcomes.if_not: a flat curve means the API ranks rather than filters

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: how recall is distributed over query length and count; no direction is asserted

claims.statement: The spread of set recall of the LLM arm over 3 sampling seeds, and of every arm over two API dates, is estimated on LitSearch questions.
reasons: a difference smaller than the run-to-run spread cannot be read as a method effect

evidence.measure: range and standard deviation of mean h over 3 seeds (temperature 0.7); change of mean h between two dates on a 150-question subset; mean h of a second, larger open model (about 3B) on the same subset
evidence.would_show: the noise floor next to the E2 difference

claims.warrant: When the same input is run repeatedly, the spread of the score is its noise floor.

outcomes.if_supported: a small spread lets single-run differences of this size be trusted
outcomes.if_not: a spread comparable to the difference means E2 must be read with it

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: how large the run-to-run spread is; no direction is asserted
claims.precision_target: 3 seeds give a range, not an interval; reported as such

sample.accessible: 597 LitSearch questions in ML / NLP, partly LLM-written from citation contexts
sample.concern: one field; some questions written by GPT-4

predictor.phenomenon: how a literature agent turns a need into queries
predictor.validity: content: the LLM arm uses the Step 1 prompt of the harness verbatim; the deterministic arm is one fixed rule among many possible

outcome.phenomenon: finding the papers the need calls for
outcome.variable: set recall against annotated gold at K x R results
outcome.accuracy: understates when unlabelled relevant papers exist [sharonhope2026]
outcome.validity: criterion: recall against annotated targets is the field's convention (ajithetal2024#E1)

tradeoffs.change: the LLM arm uses a small open instruct model instead of the harness's deployed generator (qwen3.8 under Ollama)
tradeoffs.because: data: no Ollama and no such model on this machine (probe)
tradeoffs.lost: a direct statement about the deployed generator; the measured increment is a lower bound only if stronger models write better queries, which is not tested
tradeoffs.why: the question asks about an LLM-written query set against a deterministic one; any instruct model with the same prompt instantiates it; E5 accepts recorded query sets of the deployed generator

tradeoffs.change: the verbatim-versus-keyword contrast is an estimate (C2), not a test
tradeoffs.because: the derivability screen: its direction follows from term matching
tradeoffs.lost: a pass/fail statement on that contrast
tradeoffs.why: the gap is about separating query form from the engine; the interval of C2 does that for the derivable part

tradeoffs.change: ranked metrics after LLM screening (Recall@5, MRR) are not computed
tradeoffs.because: they need an LLM relevance scorer per candidate and belong to the ranking side
tradeoffs.lost: comparability with the Recall@5 figures of the source
tradeoffs.why: the question is about set recall

tradeoffs.change: the nested deterministic rule (top-m words, m = 2..6) is no longer the comparator of the primary test; it is kept as a descriptive arm in E4, and the comparator is a non-nested rule
tradeoffs.because: reader doubt 2: nested queries conflate the LLM with query diversity
tradeoffs.lost: nothing: the nested rule is still reported, and the new comparator is the stronger one
tradeoffs.why: a stronger deterministic comparator answers the same question more strictly

reader_doubts.doubt: the decision rule (lower limit at or above 0.10) and the power statement (difference from zero) do not match; a true increment near 0.10 ends undecided
reader_doubts.how: C1 power and E2 now state the power against the threshold 0.10 (separates increments up to about 0.04 and from about 0.16 at SD 0.6) and E2 states the undecided zone as an outcome; the question was reworded to the thresholded contrast

reader_doubts.doubt: the deterministic arm's five nested queries conflate the LLM with query diversity
reader_doubts.how: E2 comparator changed to five non-nested combinations of the six highest-IDF words; E4 reports unique results per arm and the difference of C1 among questions with matched result-set diversity; a query-diversity rival was added to C1

reader_doubts.doubt: leakage: the model may have seen the gold papers and reproduce title words
reader_doubts.how: data: LitSearch contains no question about a paper published after the training cut-off of the available open models, and no post-cut-off question set is on this machine (probe: no dataset cached); E4 stratifies by question source only

reader_doubts.doubt: one roughly 1.5B model with a borrowed prompt; failure could reflect this model or malformed output
reader_doubts.how: E5 adds a second, larger open model (about 3B) on the 150-question subset and E2 reports parse failures separately and the difference with failures excluded; the deployed generator itself stays unavailable (tradeoffs row 1)

reader_doubts.doubt: the outcome is coarse and gold-biased, and questions with unresolved gold are excluded
reader_doubts.how: data: LitSearch has no relevance labels beyond its annotated targets, and judging alternatives needs a human-validated LLM judge that is not available on this machine (no hosted model, no API key); E1 reports the excluded share

reader_doubts.doubt: the mechanism (terms not in the question) and the wider significance are not tested
reader_doubts.how: the statement and Short Hypothesis call the mechanism a conjecture; the third ladder rung is marked (TBD) and listed as a risk

reader_doubts.doubt: budget matching is by result count only (the verbatim arm issues one query), and the E3 floor uses topically close questions
reader_doubts.how: E3 now has a second floor with keywords of TREC-COVID topics (unrelated field); the primary contrast of E2 compares two arms that both issue K = 5 queries, and the verbatim arm enters only the estimate C2

reader_doubts.doubt: external validity: one API with drifting results, one main dataset, a second dataset without a rule; novelty rests on titles and abstracts
reader_doubts.how: data: keyless Semantic Scholar and arXiv search were rate-limited throughout the literature stage on this machine, so a second API cannot be relied on for about 10^4 calls; TREC-COVID's many-relevant structure does not admit the 0/1 threshold
